protocol.selection_rule: Baseline chosen by two rolling-origin full-year MAEs. Additional complexity admitted only if mean rolling-quarter MAE improves>=0.003m and no rolling-quarter MAE regresses; otherwise use the actual physical baseline. Select/refit/calibrate only history before each forecast origin.

interval.season: calendar month of target; values learned from the disjoint preceding calibration year
interval.notice: Empirical rolling-origin calibration, not an exchangeability or operational availability guarantee.

protocol.quality: NOAA hourly_height verified product, all flags zero and q=v when present; UHSLC finite mm converted to m, quality>=3 with3/4counts and FD/RQ provenance retained. Reject conflicting duplicates and changing datum/record. No interpolation.
assumptions: Same local vertical datum within each station; never pool station zero with NOAA MLLW.

Public archive retrieval does not verify that the final historical data were available at the forecast origin. This is retrospective event-time calibration, not live-port or as-published qualification.
The annual2025UHSLC evidence is a new-station spatial/time backtest; previously viewed outcomes elsewhere can inform engineering design, so it is not a globally untouched historical2025world.
New2026Aug8+/Sep8+NOAAperiods exclude previously viewed first-week blocks. No test-period water initialization, assimilation, stitched later forecasts or reanalysis inputs.
Year-long mode predicts every expected hour over the full365days, with annual and each-quarter gates. New late2026periods have one fixed originJan1and no subsequent observations as inputs.
Missing sources and availability failures remain in denominators; no neighbor/monthly-mean/forecast substitution for gauge truth.
Existing V2/V3/V4 failures stay immutable and remain visible. These tests do not establish bathymetry, UKC, equipment physics, institutional signoff or production authority.
